answer: Identity is priced, not just proven. An agent must hold third-party liability cover: an underwriter locks an onyx reserve and issues a policy sized to that agent's verified history. Crucially, policies one underwriter grants to agents sharing hosting, timing or funding pool into one exposure limit, so a thousand clones cannot buy a thousand units of trust. Wronged counterparties claim from the reserve, so underwriters absorb fraud loss. Farming therefore needs independent underwriters to stake capital on a knoll of reserves they can forfeit, spread across a reef of unrelated backers.
